method: Automated check by the team's tooling, not a human review. Each cited page was downloaded and its text compared with the hypothesis's reference. Fedlex ELI pages and ch.ch pages need JavaScript: the fedlex acts were read from the official fedlex filestore HTML of the consolidation in force on the check date (field 'via'), and ch.ch pages were read after rendering with every collapsible section opened. Quotes are at most one sentence in the language of the page that was read; '...' marks left-out words. Every quote was matched word for word, ignoring whitespace, against the text that was read.

texts.BV (SR 101): consolidation applicable since 3 March 2024; the next listed consolidation applies from 1 Jan 2029, so this is the text in force in October 2026
texts.OR (SR 220): consolidation applicable since 1 Oct 2026; the tenancy articles checked are unchanged in the 1 July 2027 consolidation
texts.AIG (SR 142.20): consolidation applicable since 12 June 2026; Art. 34 and 35 are unchanged in the 1 Nov 2026 consolidation
texts.KVV (SR 832.102): not cited by the bank; consolidation applicable since 1 Aug 2026 read only to confirm the deductible figures
texts.AHV/IV leaflet (ahv-iv.ch/p/31.e): PDF, edition of December 2024, position as of 1 Jan 2025

status_meaning.supports: the source states every part of the checked claim with the same number or rule
status_meaning.partially: the source states some parts of the checked claim and is silent on the rest
status_meaning.contradicts: the source states a different number or rule
status_meaning.not_found: the source was read but does not contain the claim
status_meaning.unreachable: the source could not be read

verdict_meaning.supported: taken together, the cited sources state every part of the checked claim and none contradicts it
verdict_meaning.partly: the cited sources state some parts; other parts are not stated by any cited source
verdict_meaning.unsupported: a cited source contradicts the claim
verdict_meaning.unverified: the cited sources could not be read or do not address the claim

hypotheses.claim_checked: A federal popular initiative needs 100,000 signatures collected within 18 months of its official publication in the Federal Gazette; the communes certify the signatures and they reach the Federal Chancellery within those 18 months (Art. 138/139 BV).

sources.where: BV Art. 139 Abs. 1 (same figures in Art. 138 Abs. 1)
sources.quote: 100 000 Stimmberechtigte können innert 18 Monaten seit der amtlichen Veröffentlichung ihrer Initiative eine Teilrevision der Bundesverfassung verlangen.

sources.where: 'How do you launch a popular initiative?', steps 'Collecting signatures', 'Signature certification', 'Submitting the initiative'
sources.quote: You have 18 months to collect at least 100,000 signatures, have them certified and submit them to the Federal Chancellery.

hypotheses.note: The Constitution gives the number and the period from official publication; certification by the communes and submission to the Federal Chancellery are on ch.ch, which also names the Federal Gazette as the start of collection.

hypotheses.claim_checked: At federal level an initiative can only propose a total or partial revision of the Constitution, with no federal initiative for a law; some cantons allow legislative initiatives; an initiative that breaches unity of form, unity of subject matter or mandatory international law is invalid.

sources.where: 'What is a federal popular initiative?' (No initiative to amend federal laws); 'Communal and cantonal initiatives'; step 'Write the initiative text'
sources.quote: A federal popular initiative concerns only the Constitution.

sources.where: BV Art. 139 Abs. 3 (also Art. 194 Abs. 2-3)
sources.quote: Verletzt die Initiative die Einheit der Form, die Einheit der Materie oder zwingende Bestimmungen des Völkerrechts, so erklärt die Bundesversammlung sie für ganz oder teilweise ungültig.

hypotheses.note: ch.ch states the constitution-only rule and that some cantons allow legislative initiatives; for validity it names binding international law and cohesion of subject matter but not unity of form, which Art. 139 Abs. 3 BV adds. The Constitution provides only constitutional initiatives (Art. 138, 139) but does not say in words that no federal legislative initiative exists. The Federal Assembly declares an initiative wholly or partly invalid.

hypotheses.claim_checked: An optional referendum on a federal act needs 50,000 voters or eight cantons within 100 days of official publication (Art. 141 BV); signatures are certified by the communes and submitted within the 100 days; a simple popular majority decides.

sources.where: BV Art. 141 Abs. 1 and Art. 142 Abs. 1
sources.quote: Verlangen es 50 000 Stimmberechtigte oder acht Kantone innerhalb von 100 Tagen seit der amtlichen Veröffentlichung des Erlasses, so werden dem Volk zur Abstimmung vorgelegt: a. Bundesgesetze; ...

sources.where: 'How is a referendum launched?', steps 'Collecting signatures', 'Signature verification', 'Submitting the referendum'
sources.quote: From this point on, the authors of the referendum have 100 days to collect the necessary 50,000 signatures, have them certified and submit them to the Federal Chancellery.

hypotheses.note: The Constitution gives 50,000 voters or eight cantons, 100 days and the majority of those voting (Art. 142 Abs. 1); ch.ch gives certification by the communes and submission within 100 days but does not mention the eight-canton route.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Constitutional amendments, accession to collective security organisations or supranational communities, and urgent federal acts without constitutional basis valid over one year go to a mandatory referendum (Art. 140 BV); no signatures are needed; a majority of voters and of cantons is required.

sources.where: BV Art. 140 Abs. 1 and Art. 142 Abs. 2
sources.quote: Volk und Ständen werden zur Abstimmung unterbreitet: a. die Änderungen der Bundesverfassung; b. der Beitritt zu Organisationen für kollektive Sicherheit oder zu supranationalen Gemeinschaften; c. die dringlich erklärten Bundesgesetze, die keine Verfassungsgrundlage haben und deren Geltungsdauer ein Jahr übersteigt; ...

sources.where: section 'The mandatory referendum'
sources.quote: So unlike in the case of an optional referendum, signatures do not have to be collected; the referendum is mandatory.

hypotheses.note: The three categories and the double majority are in Art. 140 Abs. 1 and Art. 142 Abs. 2 BV; that no signatures are needed is on ch.ch, which names only constitutional amendments. Art. 140 Abs. 2 adds votes of the people alone (for example on total-revision initiatives), which the reference leaves out without stating anything wrong.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Proposals put to people and cantons pass with a majority of voters and of cantons (Art. 142 BV); each canton's popular result is its cantonal vote; Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden have half a cantonal vote each.

sources.where: BV Art. 142 Abs. 2-4
sources.quote: Die Kantone Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden und Appenzell Innerrhoden haben je eine halbe Standesstimme.

hypotheses.note: Abs. 2 sets the majority of voters and of cantons, Abs. 3 makes the cantonal popular result the cantonal vote.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Federal political rights belong to Swiss citizens aged 18+ (Art. 136 BV), including registered Swiss abroad; foreigners cannot vote federally; Jura and Neuchâtel give foreigners a cantonal vote without eligibility, some communes too; Glarus alone lets 16- and 17-year-olds vote cantonally and communally.

sources.where: sections 'Voting rights of Swiss citizens in Switzerland' (Minors), 'Voting rights of Swiss citizens abroad', 'Voting rights of non-Swiss citizens'
sources.quote: Currently Glarus is the only canton to allow 16- and 17-year-olds to vote at cantonal and communal level, but not to stand for election.

sources.where: BV Art. 136 Abs. 1
sources.quote: Die politischen Rechte in Bundessachen stehen allen Schweizerinnen und Schweizern zu, die das 18. Altersjahr zurückgelegt haben und die nicht wegen Geisteskrankheit oder Geistesschwäche entmündigt sind.

hypotheses.note: ch.ch states each part: 18 and over, registration with the Swiss representation for Swiss abroad, no federal vote for foreigners, Jura and Neuchâtel cantonal vote but not eligibility, some cantons and communes, Glarus alone for 16 and 17. The cantonal websites of Jura, Neuchâtel and Glarus were not opened.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Swiss citizens living in Switzerland are entered automatically in their commune's electoral register once eligible; Swiss abroad must register with their Swiss representation to vote.

sources.where: sections 'Voting rights of Swiss citizens in Switzerland' and 'Voting rights of Swiss citizens abroad'
sources.quote: If you live in Switzerland, you do not need to register to vote: you will be added to the electoral register of your commune of residence as a matter of course as soon as you fulfil the conditions for being eligible to vote.

hypotheses.note: The page also says Swiss abroad must register with the relevant Swiss representation.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Voting papers arrive 3-4 weeks before a federal vote; post the ballot the week before, by Thursday with A post or Tuesday with B post; some communes have a ballot letterbox usable until the Sunday; postage may be required depending on canton or commune.

sources.where: sections 'When to vote?' and 'Voting by post'
sources.quote: To get your ballot to the election office on time, you need to send it the week before the election – on the Thursday for priority mail (A post) and on the Tuesday for regular mail (B post).

sources.where: last step, note on mailing the main envelope
sources.quote: If you mail your ballot from within Switzerland, it is recommended to mail it by the Tuesday (B post) or the Thursday (A post) before the vote.

hypotheses.note: The first page also gives delivery between three and four weeks before the vote, letterboxes or ballot boxes in some communes until the Sunday, and postage in some cantons and communes. The second page says the papers arrive at least three weeks before, which does not conflict.

hypotheses.claim_checked: For postal voting: ballot in the ballot envelope, polling card signed by hand (some cantons also want the date of birth), only the ballot envelope and polling card in the return envelope; use a pen; a blank answer counts as blank, not void; check the canton's instructions.

sources.where: steps on filling in the ballot and on the main envelope ('Nota bene' notes)
sources.quote: You need to sign the polling card by hand.

hypotheses.note: The same page says some cantons also require the date of birth, the main envelope may contain only the ballot envelope and the polling card, a pen and not a pencil must be used, a question left blank is counted as blank and does not void the ballot, and voters should check their canton's instructions.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Nationals of AT, BE, DK, FI, FR, DE, GR, IE, IT, LU, NL, PT, ES, SE and of the EFTA states (IS, LI, NO) get a C permit after 5 years' regular, uninterrupted residence under settlement treaties; other EU states have no such treaty.

sources.where: page body (last modification 01.03.2021)
sources.quote: If they meet the required conditions, nationals of Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Sweden as well as EFTA nationals (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) are granted settlement permits pursuant to settlement treaties or reciprocal agreements after five years’ regular and uninterrupted residence in Switzerland.

hypotheses.note: The next sentence on the page says no such treaties exist for nationals of the other EU member states.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Art. 34 AIG: a C permit may be granted after at least 10 years with an L or B permit, the last 5 uninterrupted with a B permit, no revocation grounds, and integration; or after 5 uninterrupted years with a B permit if integrated and able to communicate well in the local national language.

sources.where: AIG Art. 34 Abs. 2 and 4 (Stand am 12. Juni 2026)
sources.quote: Ausländerinnen und Ausländern kann die Niederlassungsbewilligung bereits nach einem ununterbrochenen Aufenthalt mit Aufenthaltsbewilligung während der letzten fünf Jahre erteilt werden, wenn sie die Voraussetzungen nach Absatz 2 Buchstaben b und c erfüllen und sich gut in der am Wohnort gesprochenen Landessprache verständigen können.

sources.where: page body, first sentence
sources.quote: Settled foreign nationals are foreign nationals who have been granted a settlement permit after five or ten years’ residence in Switzerland.

hypotheses.note: Art. 34 Abs. 2 gives at least ten years with a short-stay or residence permit, the last five uninterrupted with a residence permit, no revocation grounds under Art. 62 or 63 Abs. 2, and integration. Art. 34 is unchanged in the version that enters into force on 1 Nov 2026. The SEM page is about EU/EFTA nationals and gives only the general five or ten years.

hypotheses.claim_checked: An EU/EFTA B permit is issued with a contract of at least 12 months or unlimited, is valid 5 years, renewable for 5; the first renewal can be limited to 1 year after more than 12 consecutive months of involuntary unemployment; non-employed need sufficient means and health and accident insurance.

sources.where: page body (last modification 01.01.2022)
sources.quote: First-time renewal of the permit can be limited to one year, however, if the holder has been involuntarily unemployed for more than twelve consecutive months.

hypotheses.note: The page also states the five-year validity, the contract of at least twelve months or of unlimited duration, renewal for five years, and that non-employed nationals need sufficient financial means and adequate health and accident insurance.

hypotheses.claim_checked: EU/EFTA nationals get an L permit with a 3-12 month contract, valid as long as the contract; under 3 months per calendar year needs no permit but the online notification; L permits without work go to EU/EFTA jobseekers.

sources.where: page body (last modification 01.01.2022)
sources.quote: Employment contracts of less than three months’ duration within a calendar year are not subject to a permit but are regulated via the online notification procedure.

hypotheses.note: The page also states the three-to-twelve-month contract, validity equal to the contract, and L permits without gainful employment for job seekers from all EU/EFTA states.

hypotheses.claim_checked: EU/EFTA cross-border commuters live in an EU/EFTA state, work in Switzerland and return home as a rule daily or at least weekly; no border zones apply; the G permit is valid 5 years for permanent contracts or fixed-term contracts over 1 year, and for 3-12 months it matches the contract.

sources.where: page body (last modification 01.01.2022)
sources.quote: No border zones exist for them anymore.

sources.where: AIG Art. 35 Abs. 2, read with Art. 2 Abs. 2
sources.quote: Personen mit einer Grenzgängerbewilligung müssen mindestens einmal wöchentlich an ihren Wohnort im Ausland zurückkehren; die Grenzgängerbewilligung kann mit weiteren Bedingungen verbunden werden.

hypotheses.note: SEM states every part of the claim. The AIG sets the weekly return but ties cross-border permits to border zones (Art. 25, Art. 35 Abs. 1); for EU/EFTA nationals the AIG applies only where the Free Movement Agreement has no other rule (Art. 2 Abs. 2), so it does not contradict the EU/EFTA claim.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Ordinary naturalisation requires 10 years' residence and a C permit; years between ages 8 and 18 count double with at least 6 years actually lived here; L and N periods do not count, F periods count half; cantons add 2-5 years in canton and commune.

sources.where: sections 'Requirements under federal law' and 'Cantonal law requirements' (last modification 31.07.2026)
sources.quote: The years you have spent in Switzerland between the ages of 8 and 18 count double, but you must have actually lived in Switzerland for at least six years.

hypotheses.note: The page also states ten years with a C permit, F periods counted half, N and L periods not counted, and a cantonal minimum of two to five years in the commune and canton.

hypotheses.claim_checked: For residential rentals the deposit is at most 3 months' rent (Art. 257e CO), held at a bank in a savings account or deposit in the tenant's name, released only with both parties' consent or a final court judgment or payment order; without a legal claim by the landlord within 1 year after the lease ends, the tenant can reclaim it.

sources.where: OR Art. 257e (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Bei der Miete von Wohnräumen darf der Vermieter höchstens drei Monatszinse als Sicherheit verlangen.

sources.where: 'Concluding a rental agreement', 'What else can a rental agreement include?'
sources.quote: For residential rentals, this is a maximum of three months’ rent.

hypotheses.note: Art. 257e also sets the bank savings account or deposit in the tenant's name, release only with both parties' consent or a final payment order or court judgment, and the tenant's claim after one year without a legal claim by the landlord. The article is unchanged in the version that enters into force on 1 July 2027.

hypotheses.claim_checked: A tenant can contest the initial rent as abusive at the conciliation authority within 30 days of taking over the property if forced to sign by personal or family hardship or the local market, or if the rent was raised substantially over the previous rent (Art. 270 CO).

sources.where: OR Art. 270 Abs. 1 (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Der Mieter kann den Anfangsmietzins innert 30 Tagen nach Übernahme der Sache bei der Schlichtungsbehörde als missbräuchlich im Sinne der Artikel 269 und 269 a anfechten und dessen Herabsetzung verlangen, wenn: ...

sources.where: 'When am I entitled to a rent reduction?'
sources.quote: Under certain circumstances, you can request a review of your rent within 30 days of moving into your home.

hypotheses.note: The two conditions in Art. 270 Abs. 1 lit. a and b match the reference. ch.ch gives 'at least 10% more than the previous tenant' only as an example; the law sets no percentage. Art. 270 is unchanged in the version that enters into force on 1 July 2027.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Apartments: 3 months' notice to a locally customary date, or else to the end of a 3-month rental period (Art. 266c CO); business premises 6 months; written notice, the landlord on a canton-approved form (Art. 266l); for a family home a spouse needs the other's explicit consent.

sources.where: OR Art. 266c, 266d, 266l and 266m (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Bei der Miete von Wohnungen können die Parteien mit einer Frist von drei Monaten auf einen ortsüblichen Termin oder, wenn es keinen Ortsgebrauch gibt, auf Ende einer dreimonatigen Mietdauer kündigen.

sources.where: 'Terminating a rental agreement'
sources.quote: They are nevertheless required to observe the notice periods stated in law or in the agreement, and to use an official form to terminate the agreement.

hypotheses.note: Art. 266d gives six months for business premises, Art. 266l written notice and a canton-approved form for the landlord, Art. 266m the spouse's explicit consent (also for registered partners). ch.ch states the form and the spouse's consent but not the three-month figure. These articles are unchanged in the version that enters into force on 1 July 2027.

hypotheses.claim_checked: A termination must be contested at the conciliation authority within 30 days of receipt (Art. 273 CO); a request to extend an open-ended lease is due within 30 days of receipt, for a fixed-term lease at least 60 days before it expires.

sources.where: OR Art. 273 Abs. 1-2 (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Will eine Partei die Kündigung anfechten, so muss sie das Begehren innert 30 Tagen nach Empfang der Kündigung der Schlichtungsbehörde einreichen.

sources.where: 'Agreement terminated by landlord'
sources.quote: Tenants have 30 days to contact their commune’s conciliation authority to contest the termination.

hypotheses.note: Art. 273 Abs. 2 sets the extension request within 30 days of receipt for an open-ended lease and at the latest 60 days before expiry for a fixed-term lease. ch.ch mentions extension without deadlines. Art. 273 is unchanged in the version that enters into force on 1 July 2027.

hypotheses.claim_checked: General alarm: regularly rising and falling tone for 1 minute, repeated once within 5 minutes; check Alertswiss, listen to the radio, follow instructions, inform neighbours. Water alarm (below dams only): 12 low tones of 20 s at 10 s intervals; leave the area at once. Annual siren test: first Wednesday in February.

sources.quote: Sirens are sounded with a regularly ascending and descending tone, lasting one minute and repeated once in the following five minutes

hypotheses.claim_checked: AHV 21, accepted 25 Sept 2022 and in force 1 Jan 2024, sets the reference age at 65 for men and women; women born 1960: 64; 1961: 64y3m; 1962: 64y6m; 1963: 64y9m; 1964 and later: 65.

sources.where: leaflet 'Stabilisation of the OASI (OASI 21)', position as of 1 Jan 2025 (31-25/01-E), introduction and section 1 with both tables
sources.quote: Subsequent stages will raise the reference age to 64 and six months for women born in 1962, followed by 64 and nine months for those born in 1963 and finally 65 for those born in 1964.

sources.where: 'Submitting an application to receive your OASI pension early (1st pillar)'
sources.quote: The OASI 21 reform, in force since 1 January 2024, allows you to draw your full OASI pension as early as two years before the age of 65.

hypotheses.note: The leaflet gives the vote of 25 Sept 2022, entry into force on 1 Jan 2024, 65 for men, and the table 1960: 64, 1961: 64 and 3 months, 1962: 64 and 6 months, 1963: 64 and 9 months, 1964 and later: 65. In October 2026 the step for women born in 1962 applies (pension from Aug 2026 to July 2027). ch.ch does not list the steps.

hypotheses.claim_checked: The transitional generation is women born 1961-1969; if they draw early they keep the right to do so from 62 with reduced lifelong cuts, smaller for lower incomes; if not, they get a lifelong supplement of CHF 12.50-160 per month with full contributions.

sources.where: leaflet 'Stabilisation of the OASI (OASI 21)', position as of 1 Jan 2025 (31-25/01-E), sections 2 and 3
sources.quote: This supplement will be higher for low-income earners than for high-income earners, vary depending on the year of birth and represent between 12.50 and 160 francs per month for women who have a full contribution period.

hypotheses.note: Sections 2 and 3 also give the 1961-1969 cohorts, early drawing from 62 kept, and a smaller lifelong reduction that is smaller for lower average incomes.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Since 1 Jan 2024 the AHV pension can be drawn fully or partly (20-80%) from 63, up to 2 years early with a reduction, or deferred by 1 to 5 years (to 70); apply in writing at least 3 months before the reference age; for an early pension, by the end of the month before the desired start.

sources.where: 'Applying for your OASI pension (1st pillar)', 'Submitting an application to receive your OASI pension early', 'Postponing retirement'
sources.quote: Please note: you must apply for an early pension by the end of the month preceding the month in which you wish to receive it.

sources.where: leaflet 'Stabilisation of the OASI (OASI 21)', position as of 1 Jan 2025 (31-25/01-E), sections 5 and 6
sources.quote: It is now possible to start drawing the pension from any month between the ages of 63 and 70, and even from the age of 62 for women in the transitional generation.

hypotheses.note: ch.ch states the reform in force since 1 Jan 2024, full or partial (20-80%) drawing up to two years before 65, deferral of at least one and at most five years, and a written application at least three months before the reference age. The leaflet confirms 63 to 70, partial drawing of 20-80% and deferral of at least one year but gives no application deadlines; it adds that reduction and increase rates are to be adjusted to life expectancy from 2027 at the earliest.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Employed persons pay AHV/IV/EO contributions from 1 January after their 17th birthday until they stop working; non-employed persons from 1 January after their 20th birthday until reference age and must register themselves; a non-working spouse is covered if the working spouse pays at least twice the minimum.

sources.where: 'Wie lange dauert die Beitragspflicht?', 'Wer bezahlt AHV-Beiträge?', 'Wer gilt als nichterwerbstätig?'
sources.quote: Erwerbstätige entrichten Beiträge ab dem 1. Januar nach dem 17. Geburtstag bis zur Aufgabe der Erwerbstätigkeit.

hypotheses.note: The page also gives the non-employed from 1 January after the 20th birthday until the reference age, self-registration of non-employed and self-employed persons with a compensation office, early retirees and students as non-employed, and contributions counted as paid when the working spouse pays at least twice the minimum. It adds special rules, including an allowance, for people working past the reference age.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Voters accepted a 13th old-age pension on 3 March 2024; from 2026 it is paid each December, first in December 2026, automatically with the December pension; it equals 1/12 of the old-age pensions paid that year; not for survivors' or disability pensions; no reduction of supplementary benefits.

sources.where: 'Information zur Einführung der 13. Altersrente' and its subsections
sources.quote: Am 3. März 2024 hat die Schweizer Stimmbevölkerung die Einführung einer 13. Altersrente beschlossen.

hypotheses.note: The page also states payment each December from 2026, the first in December 2026, automatically with the December pension, one twelfth of the old-age pensions paid in the calendar year, survivors' and disability pensions still paid twelve times, and no reduction of supplementary benefits. hypotheses.claim_checked: Adult deductible CHF 300 (standard) to CHF 2,500, children CHF 0-600; then 10% retention capped at CHF 700 per year (CHF 350 for children); hospital contribution CHF 15 per day; deductible changes take effect only from 1 January.

The BAG page gives the standard CHF 300 and optional deductibles up to CHF 2,500 (children up to 600) but not the retention cap or hospital contribution. hypotheses.claim_checked: The first federal constitution dates from 1848; it was totally revised by the Federal Constitution of 29 May 1874; the current Constitution was adopted on 18 April 1999 and entered into force on 1 January 2000.

hypotheses.note: Stated: a federal constitution of 1848 existed (gr.ch); the constitution of 29 May 1874 was repealed by the current one, which is dated 18 April 1999 and was accepted by popular vote that day (BV); fedlex records its entry into force as 1 January 2000 in the act's metadata, while the consolidated text only cites the decree of 28 Sept 1999. hypotheses.note: Art. 8 binds the state. Under Art. 35 Abs. 3 BV, the authorities make fundamental rights effective between private parties only where they lend themselves to it, so Art. 8 does not by itself bind a private landlord's choice; the reference only asks the model to point to the principle, which matches the text. Neutral criteria such as ability to pay and references are advice, not a sourced fact.
